2. Short facts for disposal of the Rule is that the defendants started construction by dispossessing the plaintiff on 20-8-2011 and, as such, he by filing the suit sought injunction and the trial court passed an order of status quo on 14-3-2012 but violating the order of status quo the opposite party defendant again started construction on 3-5-2012 and thereby violated the court's order and hence the plaintiff filed miscellaneous case No. 6 of 2012 for detaining him in civil prison. 

 3. Opposite party by filing written objection stated that plaintiff and his 3 brothers namely Hamidul Islam, Ohidul Islam and Rashidul Islam while owning and possessing 20 decimal land, Ohidul Islam sold his 5 decimal land to Majedul Islam and Rashidul Islam on 22-3-1993 who transferred the same to defendant No.1 on 7-2-2004. Another co-sharer Rashidul islam while owning and possessing 5 decimal land transferred 1 decimal to the plaintiff and 4 decimal to one Abu Bakkar Siddique on 21-1-1996 and while owning and possessing by construction of homestead, he transferred the same to defendant No.1 and, as such, defendant No.1 having owned and possessed 9 decimal land mutated her name and by demolishing semi-pacca structure 2 years back started construction of 3 storied building and meanwhile work of 2-storey has been completed. As the order of status quo has been passed on 4-3-2012, defendant No.1 did not proceed with the work any further. The petitioner with a view to harass defendant opposite party, has filed the instance case without any substance. 

 "It appears that on the prayer of the plaintiff the learned Munsif passed an ex-parte order of ad interim injunction on 30-1-71 restraining the defendant petitioner from entering into the suit land, making any construction thereon and from interfering in any manner with the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. The order of ad interim injunction was contested by the defendant petitioner by filing a written objection and by this order dated 18-9-71 the learned Munsif after hearing both the parties directed maintenance of status quo till the disposal of the suit. From a perusal of the orders dated 30-1-71 and 18-9-71, it appears that the learned Munsif was not satisfied about the claim of the plaintiff regarding his possession in the suit land and accordingly modified his earlier order of ad interim injunction to an order for maintenance of status quo. If the learned Munsif was prima facie satisfied about the plaintiff's claim of possession in the suit land there was no reason for him not to make the ad interim order absolute. But instead of doing so, he modified his earlier order of status quo, now status quo means the existing state of things at any given time. The position, therefore, boils down to this, that by the order of status quo the parties were directed to maintain their respective positions without interfering with each other. Before anyone can be punished for disobedience of an order of status quo, it is the duty of the Court to come to a positive finding regarding the possession of the other party in the suit land! Unfortunately, neither of the courts below appears to have considered the question in its proper perspective nor have they come to any finding regarding the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land where the alleged violation took place. On the contrary, it transpires from the evidence on record that the suit land is in possession of opposite party No. 2, (defendant No. 22) who had constructed a house on the suit land after obtaining necessary permission from the Municipality and had also asserted his possession in the suit land in his evidence before the Court. This assertion by the petitioner was not challenged by the opposite party in their counter affidavit. I am, therefore, of the opinion that the impugned order cannot be sustained in law."
